# ReplyInPublic

> ReplyInPublic is a web inbox for comments customers have already posted in public. It groups comments about the same issue. A person decides what to answer. ReplyInPublic does not post the reply.

By Pranav Kaja (https://pranavkaja.com/). Last updated 16 November 2026.
Home: https://replyinpublic.us/
This file: https://replyinpublic.us/llms-full.txt

ReplyInPublic is for brand teams that want to answer feedback customers already posted in public, rather than only collecting it through satisfaction and feedback surveys. The live inbox shows real public comments for five kitchen brands: KitchenAid, Nespresso, Breville, Instant Pot, and Ninja. Comments are read from YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X (formerly Twitter), and Reddit. A comment can be on a brand post or on a creator or community post. Opening the inbox requires a sign in. The site does not publish a price.

The product does not post a reply. A person reviews the comment, can keep a draft, and opens the original conversation to answer. It does not run a satisfaction survey. The live inbox is those five brands, not every brand.

Surveys measure satisfaction. Replies earn it.

## What is ReplyInPublic?

https://replyinpublic.us/answers/what-is-replyinpublic

ReplyInPublic is a web inbox for comments customers have already posted in public. It collects those comments, groups the ones that describe the same issue, and leaves the reply with a person. The product does not post a reply by itself. Opening the inbox requires a sign in.

It is for brand teams that want to answer feedback customers already posted in public. The point is to move attention from satisfaction and feedback surveys toward those public comments.

The live workspace shows real public comments for KitchenAid, Nespresso, Breville, Instant Pot, and Ninja, from YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X (formerly Twitter), and Reddit. A comment may sit on the brand's own post, or on a creator or community post. The inbox can filter those two apart. Comments that describe the same issue are shown together. Each comment can be parked for a reply, followed up later, or kept as feedback for the brand.

What it does not do:

- It does not post a reply.
- It does not run a satisfaction survey.
- It does not publish a price on this site.
- The live inbox is those five brands. It is not a feed of every brand.

## Public comments vs surveys

https://replyinpublic.us/answers/public-comments-vs-surveys

A survey starts with a question from the brand. A public comment starts with the customer. Nobody prompted it. ReplyInPublic is the inbox for that second kind of feedback. It is not a survey tool.

Who starts it: a survey is the brand asking a question. A public comment is the customer writing first.

Was it prompted: a survey answer was requested by the brand. A public comment was not prompted.

What it costs to collect: a survey has its own cost, and a brand sometimes gives a discount code or a similar goodie for finishing. That giveaway is a cost on top of the survey. A public comment is already public, so collecting it does not require a giveaway.

Who can see the outcome: survey answers stay with the brand, inside the survey. A reply in the thread can be seen by other people reading that post.

Where ReplyInPublic fits: it does not run the survey. It puts the comments in one inbox so a person can decide what to answer.

Public feedback is more honest, because nobody was prompted. It is already there, so the brand did not pay to collect that comment. And it is visible to everyone reading: when the brand answers, those readers see a brand that cares.

This site does not give a number for how often people finish surveys, and it does not give a dollar cost for running one. No figure of that kind is published here.

## How to answer public customer comments

https://replyinpublic.us/answers/how-to-answer-public-comments

To answer a public comment in ReplyInPublic, sign in, read the comment, check the other comments about the same issue, and choose the next step. You can keep a draft and open the original conversation. You send the reply. ReplyInPublic does not post it.

You need a sign in. The live inbox holds comments for KitchenAid, Nespresso, Breville, Instant Pot, and Ninja, from YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X (formerly Twitter), and Reddit.

1. Sign in. Open https://replyinpublic.us/ and sign in. Real public comments stay behind that sign in.
2. Read the inbox. The list is questions, complaints, and people waiting to buy. Filter comments on the brand's own posts, or earned conversations on creator and community posts.
3. Open the issue. Comments that describe the same problem sit together. One frustrated customer may be saying what others are also saying.
4. Choose the next step. Park a reply, follow up later, or keep the feedback for the brand. Keep a draft if you want one, then open the original conversation. You write and send the reply there. ReplyInPublic does not post it for you.

The inbox keeps the comment, the draft, and the next step so the queue stays clear without losing the context. Publishing the reply is a person's action on the original conversation.

## FAQ

https://replyinpublic.us/answers/faq

How is this different from a survey?
A survey starts with a question from the brand. Public feedback starts with the customer. ReplyInPublic gives those unsolicited comments a place in the workflow, so a person can act on what people are already saying.

Is it only for comments on our own posts?
No. The inbox includes comments on brand posts and earned conversations on creator and community posts. You can filter between the two.

Does it automatically post replies?
No. You decide what deserves a reply. The inbox helps you review a comment, keep a draft, track a next step, and open the original conversation. ReplyInPublic does not post the reply.

What can I explore in the inbox?
The live inbox holds real public comments for five kitchen brands: KitchenAid, Nespresso, Breville, Instant Pot, and Ninja. Comments that describe the same issue are grouped. There is a follow up pipeline and a place to keep brand feedback. Opening the inbox requires a sign in.

Where do the comments come from?
YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X (formerly Twitter), and Reddit. The live workspace is limited to those five brands.

Does the site list a price?
No. ReplyInPublic does not publish a price.
